svg.text: structural baseline d2e97b5ca · not an artistic plate · geometry is binding

g.text: 1 · WORLD FRAME
Canonical view: the nave, facing the altar.
+X epistleward → page RIGHT -X gospelward → page LEFT
+Y altarward (away from the people) -Y naveward
+Z upward
yaw 0° = epistleward, 90° = altarward, 180° = gospelward
turn right = yaw decreasing; turn left = yaw increasing.
A turn is a sense, never a fixed pair of endpoints, so the two
full-circle turns sweep correctly from a naveward start.
+X epistle
-X gospel
+Y altarward
-Y naveward
2 · MISSAL ORIENTATION
The failure this layer exists to prevent: a mirrored book.
Epistle side LM-001A mensa-epistle yaw 135.0°
Gospel side LM-035A mensa-gospel-corner yaw 135.0°
X is negative on both sides: the priest turns gospelward to read,
wherever the book stands. The mirrored value 45° never occurs.
SAME YAW ON BOTH SIDES: yes
3 · CAMERA AND PANEL CONTRACT
Projection and camera position are independent vocabularies.
LM-001A projection perspective position nave-centre
panels 1 (primary) additional_panels: forbidden
LM-136C panels 2 (primary, path-plan) — the plan is DECLARED, not invented
A plan view is projection orthographic-plan with a declared
page-top world direction. "nave" is a position and can never be
spelled as a projection, so "TOP VIEW (NAVE)" is unwritable.
UNDECLARED PANELS: forbidden, and checked against every skeleton
4 · CROSSING PRECEDENCE
Ordered choreography must survive compilation, not stay prose.
LM-136C first crossing AC2 y=0.5 (rank 1) AC1 y=0.66 (rank 2)
LM-136E second crossing AC1 y=0.5 (rank 1) AC2 y=0.66 (rank 2)
Smaller y is nearer the viewer. depth_rank compiles to an
explicit offset, so who leads is a number, not an adjective.
AC1 carries the chalice cloth gospelward; AC2 carries the Missal
epistleward. The Missal keeps its one reading yaw throughout.
AC2 LEADS FIRST, AC1 LEADS SECOND: yes
5 · FINE DETAIL AT THE ELEVATION
LM-099A — The elevation of the Host, with one ring
priest predella-centre [0.0, 1.66, 1.0] faces 90° hands holding-host | holding-host
AC1 predella-epistle [0.6, 1.5, 1.0] faces 180° hands lifting-chasuble-edge | holding-bell
AC2 predella-gospel [-0.6, 1.5, 1.0] faces 0° hands on-breast | lifting-chasuble-edge
The chasuble-lifting hands and the bell hand are explicit
actor state, so an artist cannot reassign them.
6 · ART READINESS
197 scenes · 140 art-ready · 57 blocked for art
A scene blocks when an unresolved serving-profile cue could change
something visible, or when a directional phrase names no frame.
Blocked is the safe default: an unclassified cue never makes a
scene ready. Cues are resolved by human review only, and never
from the fenced pre-v0.21 altar-server guides.
Every art-ready scene compiles with no unresolved visible geometry.
